passage:
Dear Manjula,

I'm writing because phone calls always end with me saying yes. Last month you needed a loan for a deposit, the month before a place to stay for a week, and before that my scooter for a weekend. I want to be honest: I'm glad to help sometimes, but I've started to feel used, because your messages arrive only when there's a need. When my father was in hospital there was no call.

This time I can't lend money. I won't give a long list of reasons, because the answer is simply no. I'd like to hear about your life too, not only your problems. If you want that, I'm here.

Warmly,
Devika

qa.q: What did Manjula need last month?
qa.a: Manjula needed a loan for a deposit.
Devika feels hurt and used because Manjula's messages arrive only when there's a need, and there was no call when Devika's father was in hospital.

qa.q: How does Devika set a limit in the letter?
qa.a: Devika says no to the loan without a long list of reasons and invites Manjula to share life, not only problems.

qa.q: How might Manjula read this letter?
qa.a: Manjula might feel hurt or defensive at first, but the warm sign-off and invitation leave room for a friendship of mutual care.

grounding: A friend who only calls for money, favours or a bed leaves Devika feeling used; Devika gives within limits, says no simply and asks for mutual care.

passage:
Wednesday night.

Vishal called again. Third time this year. "Bhai, just need to crash at yours for a week, the landlord's being difficult." Last time a week became a month, and he left my fridge empty and my scooter with a flat tyre.

Before that: "Bhai, lend me eight thousand till Friday." Friday was in March.

When did he last call just to ask how I am? I honestly can't remember. When Papa was ill, he sent a thumbs-up.

I felt the old guilt rise, the voice saying a good friend never says no. Then I felt tired. Used, really.

So I said it, short: "Not this time, Vishal. I can't have anyone stay." He waited for the reasons. I didn't give any. He said, "Okay, wow," and hung up.

I'm Jatin, and I'm allowed to have a small, quiet flat. I'll still wish him on his birthday. But a friend who only calls for favours isn't much of a friend.

qa.q: How long did Vishal's last one-week stay actually last?
How did Jatin feel after Vishal's call?
qa.a: Jatin felt the old guilt at first, then tired and used.

qa.q: What would you tell Jatin about the way he said no?
qa.a: He said no briefly and kindly without long explanations, and still kept the door open for ordinary friendship.

qa.q: How did Vishal react to Jatin's no?
qa.a: Vishal seemed surprised and put out, saying "Okay, wow" and hanging up.

grounding: A diary entry shows a young man whose friend calls only for money or a place to stay, who feels used and says no without long explanations.

passage:
Abhinav: hey Rukku!! 😊 long time
Abhinav: small thing, can I borrow your car Saturday? going to Lonavala with the gang
Rukmini: hi Abhinav. how are you?
Abhinav: good good. so the car?

Rukmini looked at the screen. The last three times he had messaged, it was for her car, her notes from a course, and a loan she was still waiting for. When she'd had surgery in June, he hadn't called at all. She felt something heavy and tired in her chest.

Rukmini: no, I can't lend the car.
Abhinav: oh. why? it's just one day
Rukmini: just can't this time.
Abhinav: ok 😐 thought we were friends
Rukmini: we are. I'd like it if we talked about other things sometimes too. how's your new job?
Abhinav: it's fine

He didn't write again that week. Rukmini put the phone down, a bit sad, and a lot lighter.

qa.q: Where was Abhinav going on Saturday?
qa.a: He was going to Lonavala with the gang.

qa.q: How did Rukmini feel as she read Abhinav's request?
qa.a: Rukmini felt heavy and tired, even used, remembering he only messaged when he needed something.

qa.q: How did Rukmini handle the request, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She said no without long explanations and invited a friendship with more mutual care by asking about his job.

qa.q: How did Abhinav seem to see Rukmini's no?
qa.a: Abhinav seemed annoyed and a bit wounded, replying "thought we were friends".

grounding: A chat shows a young woman whose friend only calls when he needs something, who says no without long explanations and notices the friendship lacks mutual care.
